package store

import (
	"context"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/pkg/errors"

// Role is the type of a role.
type Role string

const (
	// RoleAdmin is the ADMIN role.
	RoleAdmin Role = "ADMIN"
	// RoleUser is the USER role.
	RoleUser Role = "USER"
)

func (e Role) String() string {
	switch e {
	case RoleAdmin:
		return "ADMIN"
	default:
		return "USER"
	}
}

type User struct {
	ID int32

	// Standard fields
	RowStatus RowStatus
	CreatedTs int64
	UpdatedTs int64

	// Domain specific fields
	Username     string
	Role         Role
	Email        string
	Nickname     string
	PasswordHash string
	AvatarURL    string
	Description  string
}

	ID int32

	Username     *string
	Role         *Role
	Email        *string
	Nickname     *string
	Password     *string
	AvatarURL    *string

	Description  *string
}

message.text: I'm confirming that alongside proto-generated structs, the DB-mapped ones live in the store package, and I should also point to the driver query files.

q15.

The tables map to the store-layer model structs in the `store` package (this repo hand-writes SQL per driver rather than using an ORM, so there are no `TableName()` methods — the mapping is in the driver query files under `store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}/`).

| Table | Struct — path |
| --- | --- |
| `user` | `store.User` — `store/user.go` (line 29) |
| `attachment` | `store.Attachment` — `store/attachment.go` (line 16) |
| `reaction` | `store.Reaction` — `store/reaction.go` (line 7) |

Supporting evidence for the table names: `store/db/sqlite/user.go` uses `INSERT INTO user (...)` and `FROM user`, `store/db/postgres/attachment.go` uses `INSERT INTO attachment (...)`, and `store/db/postgres/reaction.go` uses `INSERT INTO reaction (...)`, each scanning into the corresponding struct above.

One caveat worth noting: there are also API-level types with the same names generated from protobuf (`proto/gen/api/v1/user_service.pb.go`, `attachment_service.pb.go`, `memo_service.pb.go`). Those are wire/API messages, not the database mappings.
